# Peer-graded Assignment: Course Project 1

## Loading and preprocessing the data
```{r}
## 1
# creating "data" directory
if (!file.exists("data")) {
  dir.create("data")
}

url <- "https://d396qusza40orc.cloudfront.net/repdata%2Fdata%2Factivity.zip"

# dowloading the zip file
download.file(url, destfile = "./data/activity.zip", mode = "wb")

## 2
# unziping the file
unzip("./data/activity.zip", exdir = "./data")

# reading the csv file
data <- read.csv("./data/activity.csv")
```


## What is mean total number of steps taken per day?
```{r cars}
## 1
# transforming "date" column to date type
data$date <- as.Date(data$date)

# aggregating the data frame by steps and date, removing NA values
daily_steps <- aggregate(steps ~ date, data = data, FUN = sum, na.rm = TRUE)

# plotting the date by steps in a histogram
hist(daily_steps$steps,
     xlab = "Total steps per day",
     main = "Total steps per day")

##2
# mean
mean(daily_steps$steps, na.rm = TRUE)

# median
median(daily_steps$steps, na.rm = TRUE)
```


## What is the average daily activity pattern?
```{r cars}
## 1
# aggregating the data by steps and intervals
avg_steps <- aggregate(steps~interval, data = data, FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)

# plotting the steps by interval
plot(avg_steps$interval,
     avg_steps$steps, type = "l")
## 2
# which interval has the maximum number of steps
avg_steps[which.max(avg_steps$steps),"interval"]

```


## Including Plots
```{r cars}
## 1
# x is the total number of rows and y is the number of rows without NAs
x <- nrow(data)
y <- nrow(data[complete.cases(data),])

# the number of NAs
x-y

## 2 and 3
avg_steps <- aggregate(steps~interval, data = data, FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)

new_data <- data

for (i in 1:nrow(new_data)) {
  
  if (is.na(new_data[i, "steps"])) {
    
    new_data[i, "steps"] <- 
      avg_steps[avg_steps$interval == new_data[i, "interval"], "steps"]
  }
}

# 4
## 4.1
# transforming "date" column to date type
new_data$date <- as.Date(new_data$date)

# aggregating the data frame by steps and date, removing NA values
new_daily_steps <- aggregate(steps ~ date, data = new_data, FUN = sum, na.rm = TRUE)

# plotting the date by steps in a histogram
hist(new_daily_steps$steps,
     xlab = "Total steps per day",
     main = "Total steps per day")

##4.2
# mean
mean(new_daily_steps$steps, na.rm = TRUE)

# median
median(new_daily_steps$steps, na.rm = TRUE)
```


## Including Plots
```{r cars}

## 1

# creating a new factor variable in the dataset
new_data$day <- factor(
        ifelse(
                weekdays(new_data$date) %in% c("Saturday","Sunday"), "Weekend", "Weekday"
        )
)

## 2

steps_byinterval <- aggregate(steps ~ interval + day, data = new_data, FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
 
ggplot(steps_byinterval, aes(x = interval, y = steps)) +
    geom_line() +
    facet_wrap(~ day) +
        labs( x = "5-Minute Interval",
    y = "Average Number of Steps")

```
